label: Netonix WS-26-400-AC WISP Switch
description: 1 RU managed passive-PoE WISP switch: 24x 1G RJ45 all PoE sources plus 2x 1G SFP uplinks, 110/220 VAC with a 400 W supply, 26 Gbps non-blocking.

poe.note: 400 W maximum power consumption for the whole unit, which is the only ceiling either vendor source publishes; the switch's own draw comes out of it, so the radios get slightly less than 400 W.

fabric.note: Netonix publishes 'Total Non-Blocking Line Rate' as the sum of one-directional port bandwidth (12x1G + 2x1G = 14 Gbps; 24x1G + 2x1G = 26 Gbps), not the duplex-doubled figure other vendors print as 'switching capacity'. Like for like with a FortiSwitch's 128 Gbps for 24x1G + 4x10G, these are half the number: 28 Gbps and 52 Gbps duplex.

notes: Spec sheet: 343 x 273 x 44 mm, under 4 kg, 110-240 VAC 50-60 Hz, 400 W maximum consumption, forced-air cooling with fan RPM monitoring, Vitesse core, MIPS 24K 416 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 16 MB flash, -25 to 55 C, CE/FCC/IC, 24 kV ESD. 24x 10/100/1000 plus 2 SFP, cages silkscreened 25/26. 24VH on ports 1-2 and 48VH on ports 1-6. 400 W across 24 ports is 16.6 W per port if every port is loaded at once - fine for the 8-24 W airMAX/Mimosa class this box exists for, and not enough to run 24 x 2 A 48VH loads. Passive PoE, software-configurable per port in the UI/CLI, not 802.3af/at: 24V and 48V at 1 A on pins 4,5(+)/7,8(-), 24VH and 48VH at 2 A on pins 1,2,4,5(+)/3,6,7,8(-) pairs. Current sensor per port. A port's wattage is therefore set by the voltage and current limit a human picks, which is why the port carries no wattage class here - only the unit's published ceiling does. Software from the same spec sheet: LACP/static LAG, STP/RSTP/MSTP/ERPS, port mirroring, VLAN dot1Q/QinQ/port trunking, SNMP, SMTP alerts, per-port bandwidth limiting, QoS, per-port ping watchdog, scheduled port bouncing, cable diagnostics, loop protection, DHCP snooping, IGMP snooping, flow control, storm control, multicast filtering, port isolation, auto TFTP backup on config change, UDP (Ubiquiti discovery), CDP and LLDP, ACLs plus login tarpit. Nothing in the sheet routes IP between VLANs, so this is l2-forward only. Management is HTTPS on 192.168.1.20 (admin/admin) with the host on 192.168.1.0/24, and a RS-232 serial console at 115200 8-N-1, no parity, XON/XOFF flow control, null-modem cable.
